relations.statement: For Computable as the allowed class, a source predicate with no computable total decider and a computable validity-preserving reduction into proposals yield a proposal-validity predicate with no computable total decider.
relations.hypotheses: hard : H -> Prop has no Computable total decider; reduction is Computable and satisfies hard h iff valid (reduction h); H and P are Primcodable.

relations.statement: Computable total deciders are closed under computable validity-preserving reductions: a computable decider for valid composed with the reduction would give a computable decider for hard.
relations.hypotheses: Same Primcodable and reduction hypotheses as R1.

relations.statement: For each n, the predicate that program c halts on input n (Code.eval c n has Dom) has no Computable total decider on Code.

lemmas.statement: Halting transport instance: for any n, the halting predicate (Code.eval c n).Dom has no Computable total decider (the Mathlib ComputablePred.halting_problem instance).
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem halting_transport_instance (n : Nat) : NoTotalDecider (fun d : Code → Bool => Computable d) (fun c : Code => (Code.eval c n).Dom) := halting_has_no_computable_decider n

lemmas.statement: General transport: a source predicate without a Computable decider plus a Computable validity-preserving reduction gives proposal validity without a Computable decider.

near_misses.claim: Halting undecidability transfers to every extensional property of DTM0 programs (Rice).
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Only halting is instantiated; no Rice instance and no extensional property of encoded DTM0 programs is given.

near_misses.claim: Undecidability transfers to DTM0 proposals via a computable reduction from DTM0 to Nat.Partrec.Code.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: No such computable reduction is supplied, so the transport has not been instantiated for DTM0.
